questions.stem: What are xylem vessels made of?

options.text: Dead, hollow cells reinforced with lignin

questions.explanation: Xylem vessels are made of dead cells that have lost their end walls, forming long continuous tubes. Their walls are reinforced with lignin, which provides strength and waterproofing.

options.text: The absorption of water by roots
The transport of sugars in phloem
The loss of water vapour from the leaves through stomata

questions.explanation: Transpiration is the evaporation and diffusion of water vapour from the internal surfaces of leaves, mainly through the stomata. It creates a pull that draws water up through the xylem.

questions.stem: How does transpiration help the plant?

options.text: It creates food for the plant
It creates a transpiration pull that draws water and minerals up from the roots

questions.explanation: Transpiration creates a continuous pull (tension) through the xylem, drawing water and dissolved minerals upward from the roots. It also helps cool the plant.

questions.stem: Why is lignin important in xylem vessels?

options.text: It provides strength, waterproofing, and prevents the vessels from collapsing

questions.explanation: Lignin reinforces xylem vessel walls, preventing them from collapsing under the negative pressure created by transpiration pull, and it waterproofs the walls to prevent water leaking out.

questions.stem: What happens to the rate of transpiration on a hot, dry, windy day?
questions.explanation: Hot, dry, windy conditions increase transpiration rate because heat increases evaporation, dry air increases the water potential gradient, and wind removes water vapour from around stomata.

questions.stem: Through which structures does most water vapour leave the leaf?
questions.explanation: Most water vapour leaves the leaf through stomata, which are tiny pores mainly found on the lower epidermis. Their opening is controlled by guard cells.

questions.stem: Why do xylem vessels have no end walls?

options.text: To form continuous hollow tubes for uninterrupted water flow

questions.explanation: The end walls of xylem cells break down during development, creating continuous hollow tubes that allow water to flow without obstruction from roots to leaves.
